claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit. To give you an accurate assessment, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children do you have that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit eligibility?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child I'm asking about.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that context. Great, so you have one child you'd like me to assess.

**What is your child's name?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: His name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now, to assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to understand your living situation.

**Does Alex currently live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful to know. Now I need to check a few more details about Alex.

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 17.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I need to understand your circumstances a bit better.

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have a right to reside in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I need to gather a bit more information to complete the assessment.

**Is Alex in full-time education or training (such as school, college, or an apprenticeship)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's doing an apprenticeship actually - training to be a carpenter.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. Let me gather the remaining information I need.

**Has Alex ever been in local authority care, or is he currently in any kind of care arrangement?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's never been in care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just one more question to complete the picture.

**Are you currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or is this a new claim you're considering?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: This is a new claim - I'm just trying to find out if I'm eligible.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect, thank you for that information. Let me now review the eligibility rules to give you an accurate assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided and the eligibility rules I've reviewed, I can now assess your situation for Child Benefit eligibility.

However, I need to clarify one important point before I give you my final assessment:

**You mentioned that Alex is 17 and doing an apprenticeship. Under the rules, Child Benefit can continue for children aged 16-19 if they're in "approved education or training." The guidance I've reviewed indicates that starting an apprenticeship in England would affect eligibility. Can you confirm whether Alex's apprenticeship is in England, or is it in a different part of the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's in England - he's doing his carpentry training here in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that. I now have all the information I need to provide you with my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Summary

Unfortunately, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Why?** Although Alex is 17 and living with you, he has started an apprenticeship in England. The Child Benefit rules specifically state that you'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts an apprenticeship in England. This applies even though apprenticeships are a form of training.

The rules do allow Child Benefit to continue for 16 and 17-year-olds in approved education or training, but apprenticeships in England are treated as an exception to this rule, and they end eligibility immediately.

If you have any questions about this decision or if your circumstances change, you can contact the Child Benefit Office for further guidance.
